relatedSnapshot.title: Make merging people safe and undoable
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Merging two people should lose nothing and should be reversible. This ticket replaces today's merge with one shared, safe merge that every caller uses, keeps what is needed to undo it for 30 days, and only lets people merge records they can access. The existing merge dialog keeps working on top of it; the new screen comes in the next ticket.

## Problem

* The merge deletes the losing person for good. There is no undo.
* It silently unlinks the losing person's Calendly bookings, meeting notetaker recordings, payment links and scheduled messages. Comments and My Day dismissals are left pointing at a record that no longer exists. Calls, call recordings, voicemails, texts, emails, tasks, notes and files already move correctly.
* It fails outright when both people are each the primary contact of a deal.
* It deletes the losing value of any custom field the survivor already has.
* It spreads an SMS opt-out to every phone of both people, and a do-not-contact status to the survivor, without warning.
* It writes the "merged" history entry outside the transaction, so the entry can exist for a merge that rolled back.
* It exists twice. The workflow step is an older copy that behaves differently and duplicates activity entries.
* It checks the merge permission but not access to the two specific records, so a rep limited to their own or their team's records can merge records outside that limit.

The cause is structural: many things refer to a person, each new feature added another, and the merge was never told.

## User experience

For a rep, the merge dialog looks the same after this ticket, but:

* Everything attached to the losing person now arrives on the survivor, including bookings, recordings, payment links and scheduled messages.
* Merging two people who each hold a primary deal works. Both deals are kept.
* An old link to the losing person opens the survivor.
* A merge can be undone for 30 days. This ticket delivers the undo itself; the buttons for it arrive with the review screen.
* A rep who cannot access one of the records is told they cannot merge them.

## Proposed fix

One merge function that the dialog, the workflow step and scripts all call, running inside the caller's transaction. It works from a written coverage list of everything that refers to a person, and it records what it did so the merge can be undone.

## What's included

* **One shared merge.** The merge dialog and the workflow step both call it. The workflow step stops duplicating activity entries.
* **Nothing is dropped.** Adds the missing moves: Calendly bookings, meeting notetaker recordings and their speakers, payment links, scheduled messages, comments, prospects, inbound SMS events and My Day dismissals.
* **A coverage list with a test.** Everything that refers to a person is listed and marked move, merge, delete or keep. The list covers database links, references stored as a type plus an ID (timeline events and comments work this way), and side effects such as triggers. A test fails CI when a new database link is not on the list. The other two kinds cannot be caught automatically, so the list is also a review checklist item.
* **Two primary deals.** The survivor's deal stays primary. The other deal is attached through the normal link with no primary contact, because the database allows one primary deal per person. Both deals stay.
* **Duplicates removed.** An email or phone the survivor already has is not added twice. Only active links count as "already linked".
* **Undo.** The losing person becomes a hidden shell that points at the survivor. A merge record stores what moved and the previous value of everything that changed or was dropped. Undo restores both people.
* **A merge preview.** A read-only check that returns, without changing anything, what would move (counts by kind) and which warnings apply. The review screen uses it.
* **A version check.** The preview also returns a version that covers both people and their emails, phones and deals. The merge takes that version and refuses, changing nothing, if anything it covers has changed since. A last-changed time on the person is not enough: adding a phone or email does not update it today.
* **Access checks.** Merge, preview and undo each check, when they run, that the user may view and edit both specific records.
* **Opt-outs and do not contact.** An SMS opt-out stays on the phone it was recorded for. A merge that would newly apply do-not-contact needs explicit confirmation from the caller.
* **The history entry** is written inside the transaction.

Not included: the new review screen and undo buttons, deals and companies, duplicate suggestions, and the Close import runner in ENG-14487.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Tickets explicitly grouped as parallel may start together when there is capacity, but they still keep the priority order below. Waves show the earliest dependency unlock, not a barrier: start a later-wave ticket as soon as its own blockers are complete.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: Merge two people through one shared merge that loses nothing and Keep merged people hidden everywhere and open the survivor from old links.

1. Merge two people through one shared merge that loses nothing: one safe merge for the dialog, workflows and scripts that drops nothing.
2. Keep merged people hidden everywhere and open the survivor from old links: merged and deleted people never show, and old links open the survivor.

### Wave 2: starts when both Wave 1 tickets are complete

Parallel: none.

3. Undo a merge of two people for 30 days: blocked by Merge two people through one shared merge that loses nothing and Keep merged people hidden everywhere and open the survivor from old links.

Cross-wave overlap: none.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## How it should work

* **Hidden shells never show.** Every screen, search, lookup and report that reads people ignores a merged shell. This needs an audit of the queries that read people before it ships. One known miss today: the server's phone lookup ignores deleted phone rows but not deleted people.
* **Undo restores exactly.** Merge then undo leaves both people as they were, including rows the merge deleted or created, not only rows it moved. SMS consent is the known hard case.
* **Activity after the merge stays on the survivor.** Calls, texts and notes added since are not split on undo.
* **Outside effects are not recalled.** A do-not-contact status already synced to the email provider stays synced. This is why the confirmation exists.
* **Undo can be refused.** If the survivor has since been merged again, deleted, or given a new primary deal that takes the slot the restored person needs, undo says why and changes nothing.
* **After 30 days** the shell and the stored previous values are purged. The purge only runs when nothing is still attached to the shell, and never removes business data.
* **A failed merge changes nothing**, including the history entry.
* **If exact undo cannot be achieved for some data**, the promise narrows for that data and the preview says so. An undo that quietly loses something does not ship.

## Who can do what

* Merge, preview and undo need the existing merge permission, and view and edit access to both records, checked when the action runs.
* Workflows and scripts run the same merge with the same rules, acting as the workflow or system.
* A merged shell is not visible to anyone.

## Done when

- [ ] The merge dialog and the workflow step both use the shared merge, with tests for each gap listed under Problem.
- [ ] Merging two people who each hold a primary deal succeeds and keeps both deals.
- [ ] A merge-then-undo test leaves both people exactly as they were, covering moved, deleted, created and trigger-managed data.
- [ ] A written list states what undo deliberately does not reverse.
- [ ] A test fails when a new database link to a person is not on the coverage list.
- [ ] A merged shell appears in no list, search, phone or email lookup, or report, and its old link opens the survivor.
- [ ] A rep without access to one of the two records cannot preview, merge or undo.
- [ ] An SMS opt-out on one phone does not spread to the other phones after a merge.
- [ ] The purge after 30 days is tested and refuses to run while anything is attached to the shell.
- [ ] Browser QA covers a merge from the existing dialog and a merge from a workflow.

## Open questions

* **Name 1.** Recommended default: ship behind a flag for the internal sales workspace first, then everyone, because the merge path changes for every workspace at once.

## Implementation context

* AI context.md: where the merge lives today, every gap with evidence, the undo gate from the plan review, and a suggested direction.
* This ticket has no new screens. The existing merge dialog stays until ENG-14587.

relatedSnapshot.title: Merge two people through one shared merge that loses nothing
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Merging two people, from the record page or from a workflow, moves everything on the losing person to the survivor, refuses records the user cannot access, and asks before it applies do-not-contact. Both entry points run the same merge. The losing person is still deleted after this ticket; undo comes in a later ticket.

## Problem

* The merge silently unlinks the losing person's Calendly bookings, meeting notetaker recordings, payment links, scheduled messages, prospects and inbound text events. Comments and My Day dismissals are left pointing at a person who no longer exists.
* Merging two people who each hold a primary deal fails.
* An SMS opt-out spreads to every phone of both people, and do-not-contact is applied to the survivor without warning.
* An email or phone both people have ends up twice on the survivor.
* The "merged" history entry can be saved for a merge that failed.
* The workflow step is an older copy that behaves differently and shows moved activities twice.
* A rep limited to their own or their team's records can merge records outside that limit.

## Proposed fix

One merge that the record page dialog, the workflow step and scripts all call, running inside the caller's transaction. It works from a written coverage list of everything that refers to a person. A read-only preview reports what would move, which warnings apply, and a version the merge checks before it changes anything.

## What's included

* **One shared merge.** The dialog and the workflow step both call it. The workflow step stops duplicating activity entries and gains the history entry and inbox clean-up the dialog already has.
* **Nothing is dropped.** Calendly bookings, notetaker recordings and their speakers, payment links, scheduled messages, comments, prospects, inbound text events and My Day dismissals move to the survivor.
* **A coverage list with a test.** Every link to a person is listed and marked move, merge, delete or keep, with a reason. A test fails CI when a new database link to a person is not on the list. Links stored as a type plus an ID, and trigger side effects, cannot be caught automatically, so they are listed by hand and added to the review checklist.
* **Two primary deals.** The survivor's deal stays primary. The other deal stays and is linked to the survivor without a primary contact.
* **No duplicates.** An email or phone the survivor already has is not added twice. Only active links count as already linked.
* **Opt-outs stay put.** An SMS opt-out stays on the phone it was recorded for.
* **Do-not-contact needs confirmation.** A merge that would newly apply do-not-contact is refused unless the caller confirms it.
* **History entry inside the merge.** A failed merge leaves no history entry.
* **Preview and version check.** The preview returns counts by kind, warnings (two primary deals, different owners, do-not-contact, opt-out present, names differ) and a version covering both people and their emails, phones and deals. A merge given that version refuses, changing nothing, if any of it has changed.
* **Access checks.** Merge and preview check, when they run, that the user can view and edit both records.

Not included: keeping merged people hidden everywhere and sending old links to the survivor (Keep merged people hidden everywhere and open the survivor from old links), keeping the losing person as an undoable shell, undo and the 30-day purge (Undo a merge of two people for 30 days), and the new review screen in Review a merge before it happens, and undo it afterwards.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## How it should work

* Every email and phone on both people ends up on the survivor once. Custom fields keep today's rule: the survivor's value wins.
* A failed merge changes nothing, including the history entry.
* The merge refuses, changing nothing, when the version it was given is out of date, and says the records changed.
* When do-not-contact would newly apply and the caller has not confirmed, the merge refuses and says why. The dialog then asks the rep to confirm and retries.
* Merging a person into themselves, or a person that no longer exists, is refused as today.

## Who can do what

* Merge and preview need the existing merge permission plus view and edit access to both records, checked when the action runs.
* Workflows and scripts run the same merge with the same data rules, acting as the workflow or system.

## What the user sees

* The merge dialog looks the same. After a merge, bookings, recordings, payment links and scheduled messages appear on the survivor.
* A rep who cannot access one of the records sees that they cannot merge them.
* If do-not-contact would newly apply, the dialog asks the rep to confirm before merging.
* If either person changed while the dialog was open, the rep sees that the records changed and can try again.

## Done when

- [ ] The dialog and the workflow step both use the shared merge, and the workflow step no longer shows moved activities twice.
- [ ] Each missing move listed under Problem has a test showing the row ends up on the survivor.
- [ ] Merging two people who each hold a primary deal succeeds and keeps both deals, including when the slot is held by a deleted deal.
- [ ] No duplicate email or phone rows on the survivor.
- [ ] An SMS opt-out on one phone does not spread to the other phones.
- [ ] A merge that would newly apply do-not-contact is refused without confirmation and succeeds with it.
- [ ] A forced failure leaves no history entry.
- [ ] A test fails when a new database link to a person is not on the coverage list.
- [ ] A rep without access to one of the two records cannot preview or merge.
- [ ] An out-of-date version is refused and nothing changes.
- [ ] Browser QA covers a merge from the existing dialog and a merge from a workflow.

## Open questions

* **Name 1 flag.** Recommended default: no flag for this ticket, because it keeps the losing person deleted as today and only fixes what the merge drops or gets wrong. The flag belongs to the undo ticket, which changes delete into a hidden shell.
* **Do-not-contact in workflows.** Recommended default: the workflow step refuses a merge that would newly apply do-not-contact unless a new step option allows it, and the run shows why.

## Expected outcome

Merging people loses nothing that is attached to them, behaves the same from the dialog and from workflows, and cannot reach records the user is not allowed to touch.

## Implementation context

* The parent's AI context.md lists where the merge lives today and every gap with evidence.
* Suggested shape: a function that takes the caller's transaction, the workspace, both IDs, the chosen name, title and tags, an attribution and an optional version. The current dialog sends both people's emails and phones, so moving all of them and dropping exact duplicates matches today's intent.
* The unique index on deal primary contact has no condition, so deleted deals also hold the slot.

relatedSnapshot.title: Merge deals and companies safely, and fold twin deals into one
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Deals and companies get the same safe, undoable merge and the same review screen as people. When merging two people would leave one person with a setter deal and a closer deal, the review offers to fold them into one deal.

## Problem

* Merging two deals or two companies deletes the losing record for good, with no undo, exactly as the person merge did.
* The deal merge is blocked by payments on the losing deal, which is why the 27 Sep clean-up of 1,144 twin deals had to be done with a one-off script instead of the product.
* Neither merge checks access to the two specific records.
* After a person merge, a person can hold two deals from the same journey (a setter deal and a closer deal). Today the only fix is another manual, unsafe merge.

## User experience

* **Deals.** From a deal's more menu the rep chooses Merge records and picks the other deal. The same review screen opens, titled "Merge deals": Keep and swap, the fields that differ (name, stage, amount, owner, source), and what moves (payments, notes, bookings, linked people).
* **Companies.** The same from a company, titled "Merge companies": name, website, owner, status, industry, and the people, deals and notes that move.
* **Folding twin deals.** In the person review, the two-deals warning gains a choice: "Fold into the Closer deal" (preselected) or "Keep both". Folding merges the two deals as part of the same action.
* **Undo.** The toast and the "Merged with" entry work as they do for people. Undoing a person merge that folded deals also unfolds the deals.

## What's included

* Deal and company merges moved onto the shared merge from ENG-14586: the hidden shell, the merge record, undo for 30 days, old links opening the survivor, the preview, and access checks on both records.
* A coverage list and test for everything that refers to a deal and to a company, the same way the person list works.
* Payments, payment events, recordings, meetings and tasks move with a merged deal. Nothing is deleted with the losing deal.
* The review screen from ENG-14587 for deals and companies, on both record pages.
* The fold choice in the person review.
* The workflow steps that merge deals and companies call the shared merge.

Not included: finding duplicate deals and companies (the suggestions ticket), merging deals in bulk, and any change to how new deals are created.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Tickets explicitly grouped as parallel may start together when there is capacity, but they still keep the priority order below. Waves show the earliest dependency unlock, not a barrier: start a later-wave ticket as soon as its own blockers are complete.

### Wave 1: starts when ENG-14586 and ENG-14587 are complete

Parallel: none.

1. Merge deals and companies safely, with undo: the safe, undoable merge and review screen for deals and companies.

### Wave 2: starts when Merge deals and companies safely, with undo is complete

Parallel: none.

2. Fold a setter deal and a closer deal into one when merging people: blocked by Merge deals and companies safely, with undo.

Cross-wave overlap: none.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14586: the shared merge and undo.
* ENG-14587: the review screen this extends.

## How it should work

* **Which deal survives a fold.** The deal that is further along wins by default: the closer deal over the setter deal, and an open deal over a lost one. The rep can choose "Keep both" instead.
* **Stage and owner.** The surviving deal keeps its stage and owner unless the rep picks the other value in the review.
* **Money.** Captured sale fields and payment totals on the surviving deal must be correct after the merge and after an undo. Payments are never double counted and never lost.
* **Reporting.** A folded deal counts once in pipeline and Floor Command numbers. Stage history from the losing deal is kept as history on the survivor, not replayed as new stage changes.
* **Automations.** A merge does not fire stage-change or deal-created workflows.
* **Undo** for deals passes the same gate as people: merge then undo leaves both records exactly as they were, including payments and trigger-managed fields, before undo is offered.

## Who can do what

The existing merge permission for deals and for companies, plus view and edit access to both records, checked when the merge, preview or undo runs.

## Done when

- [ ] Two deals with payments on both can be merged from the product, and every payment is on the surviving deal.
- [ ] Two companies can be merged, and their people, deals and notes are on the surviving company.
- [ ] A merge-then-undo test leaves both deals, and both companies, exactly as they were.
- [ ] Merging two people who hold a setter deal and a closer deal offers the fold, and folding leaves one deal with the combined history.
- [ ] Undoing that person merge restores both people and both deals.
- [ ] Pipeline and Floor Command totals are unchanged by a merge except for the removed duplicate.
- [ ] No stage-change or deal-created workflow fires because of a merge.
- [ ] A rep without access to one of the two records cannot merge them.
- [ ] Browser QA covers a deal merge, a company merge and a fold, compared with the attached design.

## Open questions

* **Which deals count as twins.** Recommended default: two open deals held by the same person in pipelines the workspace has marked as one journey, starting with the setter and closer pipelines. Deals in the same pipeline are offered as a normal merge, never folded automatically.

## Implementation context

* **Clickable prototype:** Record Merging Prototype. Private, so James has to share it with you. In the **View** picker at the bottom right, open "Review: companies", "Review: deals" and "Review: fold two deals". The frontend build guide is the AI context document on ENG-14587.
* The design screenshots are attached: the company review, the deal review and the fold choice.
* The 27 Sep script that folded 1,144 twin deals is the reference for what must move with a deal. It moved 973 payments, 4,739 events and 219 recordings, and had to update child rows by ID to stay fast.
* AI context.md: where the deal and company merges live today, what blocks them, and a suggested direction.

relatedSnapshot.title: Review a merge before it happens, and undo it afterwards
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Replace the merge dialog for people with a review screen that shows exactly what will happen: who is kept, which values win, what moves, and anything risky, in plain words. After merging, the rep can undo it for 30 days from a toast or from the record.

## Problem

Today's dialog shows three small cards with counts. The record you opened always wins, you cannot choose a name, owner or field value, nothing shows what will move, and nothing warns about two deals, different owners or a do-not-contact status. Reps do not trust it, and it has been used a handful of times.

## User experience

1. On a person, the rep chooses Merge records from the more menu. The dialog opens on a choose step: a search by name, email or phone, with likely duplicates listed first once suggestions exist. Choosing a person loads the review. Later, suggestions open the same screen with both people already chosen, skipping this step.
2. A large centred dialog opens. The header says "Merge people" and, when the pair came from a suggestion, why they matched.
3. The two people sit side by side. One is marked Keep. A swap button flips them. The person with the most activity is kept by default, then the one with an owner, then the older record. Each person's name, and an Open button beside it, opens that person's full record in a new tab, so the rep can look deeper without losing the choices made in the review.
4. Under them, only the fields that differ are listed, each with the kept person's value preselected. A switch shows all fields. Emails and phones are all kept, with a star to choose the primary email. Tags combine. First and last name always travel together.
5. On the right, "Moves to" lists what will arrive on the kept person, with counts, and says that links to the other person will open the kept one.
6. Warnings appear only when true, in words:
   * the person will hold two deals in different pipelines, and both will be kept;
   * the two records have different owners;
   * one record is marked do not contact, with a switch the rep must turn on before merging, because this part cannot be undone;
   * the names differ, so these may be two people.
7. The button names the outcome, for example "Merge into Name 7". The footer says the merge can be undone for 30 days.
8. After merging, a toast confirms it and offers Undo. The kept person's activity shows a "Merged with" entry saying who merged, when and what moved, with Undo merge while the 30 days last.
9. Undo asks for confirmation and says what comes back and what stays. If the merge cannot be undone, the dialog says why.

## What's included

* The review screen for people, replacing the current dialog on the person record and in the record drawer.
* Survivor default and swap, the differing-fields picker with "Show all fields", kept emails and phones with a starred primary, combined tags.
* "Moves to" counts and warnings, read from the merge preview delivered in ENG-14586. The screen never calculates them itself.
* The do-not-contact confirmation.
* The success toast with Undo, the "Merged with" activity entry with Undo merge, the undo confirmation, and the refused-undo message with its reason.
* States: loading the preview, merging (the button says how many items are moving), failed ("nothing was changed", with Try again), the record changed while reviewing (Reload), and no access to the other record.
* On a phone, the screen says "Open this on a computer", as other dense CRM screens do.
* Activation tracking through the repo's activation tracking skill: review opened, merge completed, merge undone.

Not included: merging companies and deals and the "fold into one deal" choice (next ticket), duplicate suggestions and the banner, and bulk merging.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14586: the safe merge, the preview and undo must exist first.

## How it should work

* **Stale review.** When the rep presses merge, the server checks that neither record changed since the preview was loaded. If one did, nothing merges and the screen asks the rep to reload.
* **Failure.** A failed merge leaves both records untouched and says so.
* **Undo window.** Undo is offered until 30 days after the merge, then the entry stays as history without the action.
* **Refused undo.** Shown with the reason the server gives, for example that the kept person was merged again later.
* **Closing the dialog** discards the choices. Nothing is saved until the merge runs.

## Who can do what

The Merge records action shows only to people with the merge permission. If the rep cannot access the other record, the screen says so and offers no merge. Undo follows the same rule.

## Done when

- [ ] Starting from Merge records, a rep can search for and choose the other person, and sees a loading state that says what is happening while the review loads.
- [ ] A rep can swap which person is kept, choose values for differing fields, pick the primary email, and merge.
- [ ] Each of the two records opens in a new tab from the review, and the review keeps its choices when the rep comes back.
- [ ] The counts under "Moves to" match what actually moves.
- [ ] Each warning appears only when its condition is true, and the do-not-contact switch gates the button.
- [ ] After a merge the toast and the "Merged with" entry both offer Undo, and undo restores both people.
- [ ] A refused undo explains why and changes nothing.
- [ ] A record edited during the review blocks the merge until reload.
- [ ] A rep without access to the other record sees the no-access state.
- [ ] Review opened, merge completed and merge undone events are verified landing in PostHog.
- [ ] Browser QA covers light and dark, keyboard use, and the states above, compared with the attached design.

## Open questions

* **Telling the previous owner.** The design's owner warning says the other owner "is told". Recommended default: leave notification out of this ticket and remove those words from the warning, since no owner-change notification exists today.

## Implementation context

* **Clickable prototype:** Record Merging Prototype. It is private, so James has to share it with you. It opens on a person with a possible duplicate. Use the **View** picker at the bottom right to open any state, or click through: more menu, Merge records, choose, review, merge, Undo.
* AI context.md: the frontend build guide. Where today's dialog lives, how the prototype's pieces map to this ticket and the next two, what the screen needs from the merge preview, and open questions.
* The design screenshots are attached: review, all fields, check first, do not contact, merging, failed, changed, no access, the toast, the merged record, and both undo dialogs, with dark versions of the main ones.
* The kit already carries the rule that first and last name stay together when choosing a name; keep it.
* The two attachments marked "latest" show the open links on each record card. The earlier state screenshots were taken before that was added; every state carries the same links. The choose step and the loading state were added on 2 Oct and are attached as "latest".

relatedSnapshot.title: Merge deals and companies safely, with undo
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Merging two deals or two companies becomes as safe and undoable as merging people. The rep sees exactly what will happen before merging, nothing is deleted, and the merge can be undone for 30 days.

## Problem

* Merging two deals or two companies deletes the losing record for good, with no undo.
* A deal merge is blocked when the losing deal has payments, which is why the 27 Sep clean-up of 1,144 twin deals needed a one-off script.
* Meetings and tasks on the losing deal are deleted with it.
* Neither merge checks that the rep can access the two specific records.

## Proposed fix

Deal and company merges use the shared, safe merge from ENG-14586 and the review screen from ENG-14587. The losing record becomes a hidden shell that points at the survivor, everything attached to it moves, and one undo puts both records back.

## What's included

* **Deals:** payments, payment events, recordings, meetings, tasks, notes, linked people and linked companies move to the surviving deal. Nothing is deleted with the losing deal.
* **Companies:** people, deals and notes move to the surviving company.
* **For both:** the hidden shell, the merge record, undo for 30 days, old links opening the survivor, the preview, and access checks on both records.
* A coverage list of everything that refers to a deal and to a company, with a test that fails when a new link is not on it.
* The review screen titled "Merge deals" and "Merge companies" on both record pages, with the toast and Undo, and the "Merged with" entry.
* The workflow steps that merge deals and companies call the shared merge.

Not included: folding twin deals during a person merge (the next ticket), duplicate suggestions, bulk merging, and any change to how deals are created.

Related: ENG-11262 also changes how the deal and company merge workflow steps delete the losing record. This ticket replaces that part with the safe merge.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14586: the shared merge and undo.
* ENG-14587: the review screen this extends.

## How it should work

* **Stage and owner.** The surviving deal keeps its stage and owner unless the rep picks the other value in the review.
* **Money.** Sale fields and payment totals on the surviving deal are correct after the merge and after an undo. Payments are never double counted and never lost.
* **Reporting.** A merged deal counts once in pipeline and Floor Command numbers. Stage history from the losing deal is kept as history on the survivor, not replayed as new stage changes.
* **Automations.** A merge does not fire stage-change or deal-created workflows.
* **Stale review.** If either record changed since the review loaded, nothing merges and the screen asks the rep to reload.
* **Failure.** A failed merge changes nothing.
* **Undo.** Merge then undo leaves both records exactly as they were, including payments and fields kept up to date automatically, before undo is offered. A refused undo says why and changes nothing.

## Who can do what

The existing merge permission for deals or for companies, plus view and edit access to both records, checked when the merge, preview or undo runs. Workflows run the same merge with the same rules.

## What the user sees

* From a deal's or a company's more menu, the rep chooses Merge records and picks the other record.
* The review opens titled "Merge deals" or "Merge companies": Keep and swap, the fields that differ (for deals: name, stage, amount, owner, source; for companies: name, website, owner, status, industry), and what moves (for deals: payments, notes, bookings, linked people; for companies: people, deals, notes).
* The same loading, merging, failed, changed while reviewing, and no access states as the person review.
* After merging, the toast and the "Merged with" entry offer Undo.

## Done when

- [ ] Two deals with payments on both can be merged from the product, and every payment is on the surviving deal.
- [ ] Two companies can be merged, and their people, deals and notes are on the surviving company.
- [ ] A merge-then-undo test leaves both deals, and both companies, exactly as they were.
- [ ] A test fails when a new link to a deal or a company is missing from its coverage list.
- [ ] Pipeline and Floor Command totals are unchanged by a merge except for the removed duplicate.
- [ ] No stage-change or deal-created workflow fires because of a merge.
- [ ] A rep without access to one of the two records cannot preview, merge or undo.
- [ ] The deal and company merge workflow steps use the shared merge.
- [ ] Browser QA covers a deal merge and a company merge, compared with the attached design.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Reps merge duplicate deals and companies from the product without losing payments or history, and can take a merge back for 30 days. Twin deal clean-ups no longer need scripts.

## Implementation context

* Clickable prototype: Record Merging Prototype, views "Review: deals" and "Review: companies".
* Designs: the "Merge deals" and "Merge companies" attachments on ENG-14589.
* AI context.md: where the deal and company merges live today, what must move, risks, and a suggested direction.

relatedSnapshot.title: Merge contacts already split across a voicemail thread and a text thread
relatedSnapshot.description:
Follow-up filed from **AC4** of ENG-12318, which explicitly permits it: *"If merging turns out to be more than a small job, split that into its own follow-up and say so, but do not leave it undone silently."* It is more than a small job.

ENG-12318 closes AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5 and AC6 — voicemail-created threads now record their Twilio line, and a throttled backfill repairs the rows already on disk. What it does **not** do is collapse the pairs that had already split before it landed.

### Why it was split out

Merging two `crm_message_thread` rows repoints foreign keys across **thirteen** tables.

> **Corrected twice.** It first said *nine*, naming only the AI-SDR-v2 tables from `intentClassifications` onward. It then said *fourteen*, which was one too many.
>
> **The count is THIRTEEN, verified 2026-08-06 against** `origin/main` ** at ** `1bfee6f3ce` **by four independent methods:** (1) enumerating `references(() => crmMessageThreadTable.id)` in the schema — 24 hits, of which 11 are `relations()` blocks that create no constraint, leaving 13 FK columns; (2) the `ADD CONSTRAINT … FOREIGN KEY … REFERENCES "public"."crm_message_thread"` statements in `packages/db/migrations` — 13, same table names, no inline `CREATE TABLE` FKs and no FK ever dropped; (3) distinct FK constraint names in those migrations — 13; (4) drizzle runtime metadata (`getTableConfig().foreignKeys`) over the **entire** schema — 13, split 8 cascade / 5 set null.
>
> **The fourteenth entry was a phantom:** `crmEmailTemplateUsageTable.threadId` does not exist. `crm_email_template_usage` (`packages/db/src/schema/crm.ts`) has exactly `id`, `templateId`, `userId`, `usedAt` and no thread relationship of any kind. It has been removed below. Note the "8 cascade and 5 set null" tally further down already summed to 13 — that part was always right.
>
> Method (4) is now a permanent test on the PR, so the list is checked against the live schema rather than transcribed, and a genuine 14th table would fail it. Line numbers are omitted in favour of table names, which are greppable and stable.

`packages/db/src/schema/crm.ts` **(2)**

* `crmDealTable.threadId` — set null
* `crmMessageTable.threadId` — cascade

`packages/db/src/schema/ai-sdr-v2.ts` **(10)**

* `executionRuns.threadId` — **NEW**
* `normalizedInboundMessages.threadId` — **NEW**
* `agentExecutions.threadId` — **NEW**
* `intentClassifications`, `dataExtractions`, `slotMatchmakingResults`, `bookingValidations`, `knowledgeQueries`, `scheduledFollowupTable`, `copywriterScoresTable`

`packages/db/src/schema/scheduling.ts` **(1)**

* `schedulingExternalBookingTable.threadId` — **NEW**

### ⚠️ Getting this list wrong loses data SILENTLY, it does not error

Of the 13 FK columns, **8 are** `onDelete: 'cascade'` and **5 are** `onDelete: 'set null'`.

So if the merge deletes the loser thread before repointing every one of them, Postgres does not raise — it **cascades the deletes** (destroying that thread's AI-SDR execution history, intent classifications, scheduled follow-ups and so on) and **nulls the rest**. A table left off the list fails quietly and looks like a clean merge.

**Therefore: repoint every FK first, verify zero rows still reference the loser, and only then delete it.** Do not rely on the FK actions to do anything useful here — they are the hazard, not the mechanism. A test should assert the row *counts* survive the merge on at least one cascade table and one set-null table, not merely that the survivor looks right.

It must also pick a survivor, recompute `messageCount` / `unreadCount` / `isRead` / `snippet` from the merged message set, and respect the `crm_message_thread_sendblue_unique_idx` partial unique index. That is a different concern from the one-line source fix, and putting a destructive multi-table data migration inside an Urgent bug fix would have made both harder to review.

### The population is small, and that is time-limited

The defect only became reachable when #5900 merged (2026-08-05 16:24Z) — before that, outbound never created threads at all. So the already-split set is whatever has accumulated since that merge, not a historic backlog. **The sooner this lands, the smaller the job.**

### Sequencing — this should land before the predicate is tightened

ENG-12318's PR is steps 1 and 2 of three. Step 3 tightens the voicemail thread *lookup* (`apps/web/lib/services/inbound-voice-processor.ts:1118-1126`) to include the line, and must not merge until the backfill has actually **run** in every workspace. This merge job belongs in the same window.

### Additional hazard surfaced by review — worth folding in here

Once the backfill sets a line on a voicemail thread, a contact that is already split has **two** rows satisfying the outbound recorder's thread lookup, which is `LIMIT 1` with **no** `ORDER BY`:

* `apps/web/lib/services/outbound-message-recording.ts`, `findOrCreateOutboundThread`'s `byContact` query
* `apps/web/lib/services/inbound-sms-processor.ts:355-367`, `findOrCreateSmsThread` — same shape

Which row wins is therefore not contractual, so an inbound reply and the rep's outbound text can land on different halves of the split. Before the backfill the voicemail thread never matched, so the choice was at least deterministic. Merging removes the ambiguity at the root; if this ticket is delayed, add a deterministic `ORDER BY` to **both** lookups as an interim measure.

### Acceptance criteria

1. Contacts with both a voicemail-created and a text-created SMS thread on the same line are merged into one, and the count merged is reported.
2. Every foreign key in the **thirteen** tables above is repointed at the survivor before the loser row is deleted; nothing is orphaned, cascade-deleted or nulled. A test covers at least one `cascade` table and one `set null` table by asserting row counts are unchanged after the merge.
3. `messageCount`, `unreadCount`, `isRead`, `snippet` and `lastMessageAt` are recomputed on the survivor from the merged message set.
4. The sendblue partial unique index is respected — the merge never leaves two live rows sharing `(organization_id, sendblue_thread_id)`.
5. Throttled the same way as the ENG-12318 backfill (~10-12 executions/min/workspace) and safe to re-run.
6. Tests cover merging a voicemail thread and a text thread for the same contact and line, including the foreign-key repointing.

relatedSnapshot.title: Personalize emails and texts with reliable merge variables
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Reps insert person, company, owner, sender and custom-field values into reusable messages, preview the actual message for a person, and supply fallback text where needed. The same rules apply to email and SMS.

## User experience

Both template editors and all CRM email/text composer entry points offer a labelled variable picker and per-variable fallback editor. Namespaced tokens remain copyable. Preview shows the selected person, sender and company context; SMS shows the rendered length and segments. Missing values without defaults block sending and explain how to fix them.

## What's included

* `contact.name`, `contact.first_name`, `contact.last_name`, `company.name`, `contact.primary_email`, `contact.primary_phone`, `owner.name`, `sender.name`, and person/company custom fields referenced by stable definition IDs.
* Syntax such as `{{contact.first_name | default: "there"}}`; an intentionally empty fallback is allowed. Preserve valid false/zero custom values and render selected-option labels rather than IDs.
* Email subject/body and SMS body support, selected-person preview, send/schedule validation and safe HTML/text escaping. No full Liquid language, arbitrary expressions, URL/attribute interpolation or AI-generated variables.
* A saved-template selector in Conversations SMS replies, which current main lacks, plus the existing contact/call/deal/draft entry points that reuse shared composers.
* Explicit legacy-literal versus merge-format compatibility; old templates and already-scheduled messages never silently gain new evaluation behaviour.
* Team-template mode for email and SMS workflow steps, retaining existing raw-text mode.

## Blocked by

Store and preserve separate first and last names and Keep personal templates and share them with the team. The Sales Team backfill is not a blocker. UI designs are in progress and will be attached later.

## How it should work

Use the sole linked company automatically. For several companies, manual preview/composition requires a permitted linked company selection or defaults. Workflow company variables require an explicit linked company reference when ambiguous. No arbitrary first-company choice or new primary-company field.

Manual Send/Schedule blocks for missing variables without defaults and for malformed/unknown tokens. A workflow stops before dispatch with an actionable error; correction can be retried. Preview authorization respects the selected person, company, field and sender. Saved templates retain tokens, not the selected person's resolved data.

Scheduled one-off messages store the exact reviewed rendered subject/body. Workflows resolve when a send step first executes, persist one rendered claim under workspace/execution/step occurrence, and reuse it for retries. Bind stable email/SMS send identities to the claim and reconcile uncertain results before resend. Template changes cannot create a new body under an already claimed operation. Existing consent and sender/record access checks still run before dispatch.

## Done when

- [ ] Every catalogue variable and default behaves identically in both editors, preview and the relevant send/schedule paths.
- [ ] Person/sender/company switching invalidates stale preview while preserving manual edits; unauthorized IDs never expose values.
- [ ] Unknown/deleted fields, missing values, false/zero, multi-company ambiguity, unicode, HTML-like values and rendered SMS limits are covered by tests.
- [ ] Both email and SMS template workflow modes reject personal/cross-workspace/deleted templates and preserve the resolved message and send identity on retries.
- [ ] Scheduled content remains unchanged after contact/template edits, and sent history remains immutable.
- [ ] Missing-value failures are recoverable without advancing the workflow or creating a provider request.
- [ ] Browser QA covers settings, email new/reply/draft entry points, contact SMS, Conversations SMS reply, defaults, preview and scheduling; verified activation tracking is present. UI designs will be attached when James completes them.

## References

Combine Close's namespaced tags and defaults, Name 8's attribute chips, fallbacks and recipient preview, and Name 9's linked-record tokens. Team-only workflows follow Close's explicit workflow rule; do not claim Attio/Octolane document the same private-template restriction.

Preserve the protection delivered by safe email template previews. Attachments and signatures remain in their separate messaging scopes.

## Delivery order and design status

Pickup rank 3; earliest dependency wave 2. Starts after names and personal/team templates. May overlap the Sales Team backfill.

James is designing the UI. Create and plan this ticket now; attach the matching designs later. Backend/data work can proceed. Final visible controls must follow the completed designs before UI sign-off. CRM redesign handover.

## Implementation context

AI context.md contains the full variable catalogue, grammar, rendering, permission, scheduled-message and workflow retry contracts.

relatedSnapshot.title: Stop showing "Texting is unavailable" while the text box is still checking
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a rep opens the text box on a person or deal, they sometimes see a red "Texting is unavailable. SMS is unavailable while consent status cannot be verified. Try again shortly." notice that disappears by itself. Nothing is actually wrong: the app is still checking whether the person accepts texts. This ticket shows that wait as a wait, and keeps the red notice for real problems, with a way to retry.

## Problem

Reported on the 30 Sep migration call: the notice showed for up to a minute on load, then went away. It looked like texting was broken during the busiest week of the move from Close.

Checked on main on 1 Oct: the text box treats "still checking" and "the check failed" as the same thing and shows the outage wording for both. The check retries quietly three times, so when the database is slow (the Close import was running) the wait, and the red notice, can last close to a minute. So this is not only a side effect of the import. Any slow moment shows a false outage.

The same wording also appears when retrying can never help, for example when the person was deleted or the rep is not allowed to see them.

## User experience

* **Checking:** the text box is disabled and says "Checking whether you can text this person…". No red notice. Sending stays blocked until the check finishes.
* **Check failed:** a notice says "We couldn't check whether this person accepts texts." with a Retry button. It no longer says "try again shortly" with nothing to press.
* **Not allowed or not found:** the notice says the rep cannot text this person, with no Retry.
* **Opted out or do not contact:** unchanged, these already have their own clear messages.

This applies to the text box on person and deal records (page and drawer), the in-call text box, and the first-text box in Conversations. The reply box in Conversations already behaves correctly.

## What's included

* The loading, failed and not-allowed states above on every surface that shows the notice today.
* Sending stays blocked while the answer is unknown. A text must never go out before the consent check has passed.
* Fewer silent retries, so a real failure shows within seconds instead of after a minute.
* Not included: making the consent check itself faster. It runs several database reads each time the box opens. If the notice still appears often after this change, that is a separate performance ticket.

## Done when

- [ ] With the consent check held open, the text box shows the checking state and no red notice, and Send is disabled.
- [ ] With the check failing, the notice offers Retry, and Retry re-runs the check and recovers when it succeeds.
- [ ] A person the rep cannot access, or a deleted person, shows a "cannot text this person" message without Retry and without "try again shortly".
- [ ] Opted-out and do-not-contact messages are unchanged.
- [ ] No text can be sent while the check is loading or failed.
- [ ] Browser QA covers a person page, a person drawer, a deal and the Conversations first-text box with the request blocked and then restored.

## Implementation context

* The cause is in `apps/web/hooks/use-contact-sms-consent.ts` (about lines 62 to 73): `consentUnavailableReason` returns the outage message for `isError || isPending`. The sibling `actionDisabledReason` in the same hook already separates the two ("Checking SMS consent").
* Rendered by `TextBlockedNotice` in `apps/web/components/crm-v2/record/record-composer.tsx` and by the first-text body in `apps/web/components/crm-v2/conversations/composer-text.tsx`. The Conversations reply notice in the same file already has a Retry pattern to copy.
* The query has no retry override, so the default three retries with back-off apply. The text box is mounted hidden from page load, so the check is often mid-retry when the rep opens Text.
* Several callers read `consentUnavailableReason` (`use-contact-sms-composer.ts`, the legacy Calls and Texts tab). Review them together when its meaning changes.
* Tests that pin today's behaviour and need updating: `tests/hooks/use-contact-sms-consent.test.tsx` and `tests/components/crm-v2/record/record-composer.test.tsx`.
* Not verified: the exact duration on 30 Sep. The one minute figure fits three slow attempts plus back-off but was not reproduced.

relatedSnapshot.title: The text box grows as you type on person and deal records
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a rep writes a long text from a person or deal record, the box grows with the message, the same way it already does in Conversations. Today it stays two lines tall and the rep has to scroll inside it to read what they wrote.

## Problem

Reps in AI Acquisition Sales Team mostly text from the open person or deal, straight after speaking to them. On the 30 Sep migration call a rep pasted a long message into the text box on a person and could only see two lines of it. The growing box shipped for Conversations in ENG-14469, but the record uses a separate text box that never got it.

## User experience

* A rep opens a person or a deal (full page or the side drawer), picks Text and types or pastes a long message.
* The box grows line by line up to about a third of the screen height, then scrolls inside itself. It shrinks back when text is deleted or the message is sent.
* The Send button stays at the bottom right of the box as it grows.
* The same happens in the text box shown during a call (call dock and Power Dialler wrap-up), because it is the same box.

## What's included

* Person page, person drawer, deal page, deal drawer and the in-call text box.
* The same growth limits as Conversations, so both feel identical.
* The length counter and the "too long to send" guard from Conversations (1,600 characters), since long texts are the point of this change. Today the record only shows a raw character count.
* Not included: the "open larger editor" dialog on records, bold or italic in texts, and any change to Conversations.

## Done when

- [ ] On a person page, a person drawer, a deal page and a deal drawer, pasting a 1,200 character text grows the box to its cap and then scrolls inside it.
- [ ] Deleting the text or sending it returns the box to its starting height.
- [ ] Switching between Note and Text and back keeps the right height for the draft.
- [ ] The in-call text box behaves the same.
- [ ] A text over 1,600 characters cannot be sent from a record and says why.
- [ ] Conversations behaves exactly as before.
- [ ] Browser QA covers the four record surfaces in light and dark at desktop widths.

## Implementation context

* Confirmed on main (777dba91ca, 1 Oct): Conversations uses `ComposerTextarea` (`apps/web/components/crm-v2/conversations/composer-textarea.tsx`), which fits its height to the text (36% of the viewport, 320px cap, refits on width change). Records use a hand-written `<textarea rows={2}>` with `max-h-40` in `TextComposer` (`apps/web/components/crm-v2/record/record-composer.tsx`, about line 362), with no resize code. Person, deal and the in-call composer all render that one component, so one change covers every surface. Company records have no text box.
* Suggested direction: move the fit-height logic into a shared hook that both text boxes call, instead of copying it. Swapping in `ComposerTextarea` directly would double the border inside the record's well and lose the focus handling.
* The hidden Text tab has zero width until shown, so the refit on resize must stay.
* Sequence after Acquisity/Acquisity#6756 (ENG-14549) merges: it edits the same text box (attach files, keep the box editable while sending) and does not add growth.

relatedSnapshot.title: Let the contact text box grow with longer messages
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

On a contact's Calls & Texts tab the box where a rep types a text is a single line. A longer message scrolls sideways out of view, so the rep can only see a fragment of what they are about to send. The box should grow as they type, up to a sensible height, and then scroll inside itself.

## Problem

A rep writing a follow-up text of a few sentences loses sight of the start of their message as soon as it is wider than the box. Reading it back before sending means scrolling the cursor left and right. Saved templates written over several lines are also flattened into one line when inserted, because the box cannot show line breaks.

## User experience

* The box starts at one line, as now.
* As the rep types, it grows one line at a time so the whole message stays visible, up to roughly seven lines.
* Beyond that it stops growing and scrolls inside itself, so the send and template controls never move off screen and the message history above keeps its space.
* Enter still sends. Shift+Enter starts a new line, matching the Conversations reply box.
* When a message is sent or the draft is cleared, the box shrinks back to one line.
* Inserting a saved template keeps its line breaks instead of replacing them with spaces, and the text goes out exactly as it appears in the box.

## What's included

* The contact record text box on the Calls & Texts tab grows and caps like the Conversations SMS reply box already does.
* Template insertion keeps line breaks.

Not included: the Conversations reply box (already behaves this way), email composers, and any change to how texts are sent, scheduled or recorded.

## Done when

- [ ] Typing a message longer than one line makes the box grow to fit, up to about seven lines.
- [ ] A message longer than that scrolls inside the box; the Send, template and Send later controls stay in place.
- [ ] Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a new line.
- [ ] After sending, the box returns to a single line.
- [ ] A multi-line template is inserted with its line breaks and sends with them.
- [ ] Light and dark mode both look right, and the existing behaviour when texting is unavailable is unchanged.
- [ ] Browser QA covers the points above.

relatedSnapshot.title: Undo a merge of two people for 30 days
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A merge of two people can be undone for 30 days. Instead of deleting the losing person, the merge keeps them as a hidden record that points at the survivor and records exactly what it changed, so undo can put both people back as they were. This ticket delivers the undo itself; the buttons for it arrive with the review screen.

## Problem

* A merge deletes the losing person for good, so a wrong merge cannot be taken back.
* The merge drops some data on purpose, such as the losing person's custom field value when the survivor already has one, with no record of what it was.

## Proposed fix

The merge keeps the losing person as a hidden shell and writes a merge record holding what moved and the previous value of everything it changed, deleted or created. Undo uses that record to restore both people. After 30 days a scheduled job removes the shell and the stored values.

## What's included

* **Hidden shell instead of delete,** behind a rollout flag.
* **A merge record** with the survivor, the shell, who merged, when, the expiry, what moved, and the previous value of every changed, deleted or created row.
* **Undo** that restores both people exactly, with record-level access checks when it runs.
* **Refusals.** Undo says why and changes nothing if the survivor has since been merged again, deleted, or given a primary deal that takes the slot the restored person needs.
* **The 30-day purge.**
* **A written list** of what undo deliberately does not reverse.
* **A preview warning** for any data where exact undo is not possible.

Not included: the undo buttons and review screen in Review a merge before it happens, and undo it afterwards, and deals and companies.

## Blocked by

* Merge two people through one shared merge that loses nothing, because undo records what that merge does.
* Keep merged people hidden everywhere and open the survivor from old links, because shells must never show anywhere before the merge starts creating them.

## How it should work

* Merge then undo leaves both people exactly as they were, including rows the merge deleted or created and data kept up to date by database triggers.
* Calls, texts, notes and other activity added to the survivor after the merge stay on the survivor.
* Effects outside the app are not recalled. A do-not-contact status already synced to the email provider stays synced.
* An undo that would quietly lose something does not ship. If exact undo is not possible for some data, the promise narrows for that data and the preview says so.
* The purge removes a shell and its stored values only when nothing still points at the shell, and never removes business data.
* With the flag off, the merge deletes the losing person as before and records no undo data.

## Who can do what

* Undo needs the existing merge permission plus view and edit access to both records, checked when it runs.
* Workflows and scripts create the same merge record, acting as the workflow or system.
* A merged shell is not visible to anyone.

## What the user sees

Not applicable: this ticket adds no screens. The merge dialog looks the same, and undo is reached through the review screen in the next ticket.

## Done when

- [ ] A merge-then-undo test leaves both people exactly as they were, covering moved, deleted, created and trigger-managed data, including text consent.
- [ ] Undo is refused, changing nothing, in each refusal case.
- [ ] A rep without access to one of the two records cannot undo.
- [ ] Activity added after the merge stays on the survivor after undo.
- [ ] A written list states what undo deliberately does not reverse.
- [ ] The purge is tested, runs after 30 days, and refuses while anything is attached to the shell.
- [ ] With the flag off, the merge behaves as it did before this ticket.
- [ ] Browser QA covers a merge with the flag on, then an undo through the server, then both records opening correctly.

## Open questions

* **Name 1.** Recommended default: flag on for the internal sales workspace first, then everyone.
* **Text consent.** Recommended default: store complete previous copies of the consent rows so undo is exact. If that cannot be made exact, narrow the promise for consent and say so in the preview.

## Expected outcome

A wrong merge of two people can be fully taken back for 30 days, and nothing about it lingers after that.

## Implementation context

* The parent's AI context.md has the undo gate from the plan review and a suggested direction.
* The new merge record table needs a line in the preview data copy script plus its orphan clean-up.
* The purge is a scheduled background job using the shared cron helper.

relatedSnapshot.title: A voicemail and a text from the same number split into two separate conversations
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12173. For THIS ticket: when someone leaves a voicemail, we store it as a message in a conversation thread. When a rep later texts that same person from the same number, the code cannot find that existing thread, so it creates a second one. The rep ends up with the same person in two separate conversations. Why it matters: a closer looking at a contact sees a fragmented history, and the more they use the product the worse it gets.

**Size:** S/M · **Design:** none · **Blocked by:** nothing (ships right behind ENG-12251)

### How it was found

Elis found this while auditing PR #5900 on ENG-12251 and flagged it rather than fixing it inside an unrelated PR, which was the right call. He raised it because the underlying question looked like a product decision. **James has settled it: a voicemail and a text with the same person on the same number are one conversation, and this is a bug.**

### The defect

Deterministic, not a race. No concurrency needed.

* `InboundVoiceProcessor` (`apps/web/lib/services/inbound-voice-processor.ts:1114-1147`) creates the thread for a voicemail with `sourceType: 'sms'` and `sourceProvider: 'twilio'`, and **never sets** `twilioPhoneNumber`. Its own lookup omits the line too, so it is self-consistent and never noticed.
* The outbound recorder's thread lookup requires `eq(twilioPhoneNumber, ourLine)` (`outbound-message-recording.ts:534`). A voicemail-created thread has that column empty, so the predicate can never match it.
* Result: the first outbound text to a person who has left a voicemail always creates a second thread.

**This becomes reachable the moment** ENG-12251 **(PR #5900) merges**, because before that PR outbound never created threads at all. It is not a pre-existing production symptom, it is one that arrives with that merge, which is why it should land close behind it.

### Fix

Two options were on the table. **Take the first.**

1. **Make the voicemail path record the line it came in on.** Fixes the data at the source, keeps the outbound predicate strict, and means anything else reading threads by line also starts working. Preferred.
2. Loosen the outbound predicate to also match threads with an empty line. Rejected: it hides bad data rather than fixing it, and a thread with no line recorded is wrong regardless of who reads it.

Also needed:

* **Backfill existing voicemail-created threads.** Going forward-only leaves every historic voicemail thread still splitting. Derive the line from the voicemail's own message rows or the linked call record. Where it genuinely cannot be derived, leave it empty rather than guessing, and report the count.
* **Merge threads that have already split** where a voicemail thread and a text thread exist for the same contact and line. Report how many were merged. If merging turns out to be more than a small job, split that into its own follow-up and say so, but do not leave it undone silently.
* Throttle the backfill. The job queue absorbs roughly 10 to 12 executions per minute per workspace.

### Scope

* In: recording the line on voicemail-created threads, the backfill, merging already-split threads, tests covering voicemail-then-text on the same number.
* Out of scope: the Conversations tab itself (ENG-12277), and any change to how voicemails are stored beyond the missing line. Note that voicemails are filed with `sourceType: 'sms'`, which is odd but is not what this ticket is fixing.

### Acceptance criteria

1. A voicemail followed by an outbound text to the same person on the same number lands in **one** thread, not two.
2. That holds in both orders: voicemail first then text, and text first then voicemail.
3. Existing voicemail threads are backfilled with their line where it can be derived, and left empty rather than guessed where it cannot. The counts are reported.
4. Contacts already split across two threads are merged, with the count reported, or the remaining work is split into a named follow-up.
5. A voicemail on a line with no rep assigned still records the line.
6. A test covers the voicemail-then-text case so this cannot regress.

### Design (Name 12)

Data-merge ticket — for reference, how a unified thread should render once voicemail and text land in one conversation: 38 · conversations — call thread and 19 · conversations — default + call detail.
